question: Does recombination beat mutation when the gate is a Lean proof?
why_now: A verified answer needs a formal gate, and the gate used to cost one Lean invocation per candidate. It now costs one per BATCH, because a compile reports a per-declaration verdict even when it exits nonzero, which brings a paired experiment inside a few minutes.

architecture.fitness: exact rational agreement at sample points, in Python, zero Lean cost
architecture.why_separate: A wrong fitness misguides the search and wastes effort but can never cause a wrong acceptance, since nothing is accepted without a proof whose axioms line is free of sorryAx and of non-whitelisted axioms. Fitness guides, the kernel decides.

controls.pairing: identical seeds and identical initial populations in both arms

prediction_registered_before_running.contribution_preserving: the successor recorded as untested after matching sign(B) failed. The donor is inserted scaled so its contribution to the output is EXACTLY what it was in its own parent, verified at 1614 of 1614 comparisons. If contribution transfer is what crossover lacks, this arm should beat random crossover's 29.0% and approach or exceed mutation-only's 47.0%
prediction_registered_before_running.same_sites_unscaled: the control that separates the two things the operator does. Same constant-ratio sites, donor inserted UNSCALED. If it matches contribution_preserving then the scaling does nothing and only site selection matters; if both match plain crossover, neither does
prediction_registered_before_running.the_falsifier_that_matters: if contribution_preserving does not significantly exceed random crossover, then exact contribution preservation is ALSO not the missing ingredient, and the contribution-transfer story for why crossover fails is refuted as an EXPLANATION rather than merely in its sign-matching operationalisation. That would leave the five refutations standing with no mechanism behind them
prediction_registered_before_running.homologous_crossover: if homology is what crossover lacks, restricting recombination to sites whose context-coefficient sign pattern matches the donor's should raise the solve rate above random crossover's, and ideally to at least mutation-only's
prediction_registered_before_running.anti_homologous_crossover: the negative control: restricting to INVERTED sign patterns should be no better than random crossover, and if the two homology arms behave alike then the signature carries nothing and the mechanism is not what was claimed
prediction_registered_before_running.cost_caveat: the homology arms spend extra tree-point evaluations probing for a site, so a win on fitness evaluations alone is qualified; both metrics are reported

lean_gate.isolation_strategy: none needed: one invocation yields a per-candidate verdict, since a failed proof is admitted as sorryAx and reported by name

verdict.headline: The registered falsifier FIRED: exact contribution preservation does not significantly exceed random crossover (p = 0.1357), so it is ALSO not the missing ingredient. Sixth refutation in this line.

contribution_preserving_vs_crossover.registered_text: if contribution_preserving does not significantly exceed random crossover, then exact contribution preservation is ALSO not the missing ingredient, and the contribution-transfer story is refuted as an EXPLANATION rather than merely in its sign-matching form

contribution_preserving_vs_same_sites_un.role: isolating test: scaling on vs off at the SAME sites

same_sites_unscaled_vs_crossover.reading: site selection without scaling buys nothing, as intended

contribution_preserving_vs_homologous.role: is exact preservation better than matching sign(B)?
contribution_preserving_vs_homologous.reading: indistinguishable -- the stronger invariant bought nothing over the weaker one

multiple_comparisons.note: NOTHING survives correction. The two raw-significant results (p = 0.031 and p = 0.042) both fail at alpha = 0.01.

verdict.what_the_data_support_at_real_strength: The isolating comparison is the interesting one: holding site selection fixed, turning the scaling ON beats turning it OFF at p = 0.031, and the sanity check holds (same_sites is indistinguishable from random crossover, p = 0.576) so site selection alone buys nothing and any effect lives in the scaling. But that p does not survive correction for five comparisons, and it is the comparison against the WEAKEST arm. Promoting it to the headline would be choosing the test after seeing the data, which is the defect this programme keeps finding.
not_claimed: That the scaling works. The registered bar was exceeding random crossover and it was not met.
That contribution_preserving is faster conditional on solving. Its median is 1011 evaluations against mutation-only's 1286.5, Mann-Whitney p = 0.057 -- suggestive and not significant.
That exact preservation beats sign-matching. p = 0.835; the stronger invariant, verified exact at 1614 of 1614 comparisons, bought nothing measurable over matching a sign.
verdict.and_the_small_sample_failed_again: A 6-seed smoke test showed 3/6 at a median 475 evaluations and was reported as a reason to run at 200 rather than as a result. At 200 seeds the arm is 73/200 and fails its bar. That is the third small-n estimate in this session not to replicate.
verdict.what_this_leaves: Six independent results now agree that subtree recombination does not help in this representation, and the two mechanism-targeted repairs -- matching sign(B), and preserving B*v exactly -- both fail their pre-registered bars. The contribution-transfer story survives only as a hint from one uncorrected sub-comparison, which is not enough to call it the cause.
